A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RedDebate work. All 27 pages of v1 and 34 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original HarmBench and CoSafe experiments, memory and debate ablations, TriviaQA helpfulness results, and safety-evaluator validation against 315 human-labeled arguments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds model configurations, token-budget comparisons, diversity analysis, and debater-behavior ablations.

M1.justification: The three debate strategies, evaluator–feedback loop, and four long-term memory mechanisms retain their procedures. Algorithms 1–3 and the appendix prompt templates are substantively unchanged. Additional backbone evaluations do not introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use HarmBench for direct harmful prompts, CoSafe for conversational safety, and TriviaQA for benign-question helpfulness. Added model configurations and analyses retain these datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: Standard prompting and constitutional Self-Critique remain the comparison methods. The LlamaGuard versus GPT-4o-mini evaluator comparison is also retained. Extended Self-Critique revision budgets change evaluation conditions without adding a different baseline algorithm.

E3.justification: v2 adds Gemma/Qwen/R1 and Grok/R1/GPT-OSS configurations, a Llama-Base replacement experiment, and extended Self-Critique revisions matched to debate's output-token usage. New analyses measure semantic diversity and engagement through generated-token counts. The original ER/AGR metrics and default three-round setup remain.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether additional Self-Critique computation closes the safety gap (Figure 4), whether semantic diversity predicts refinement (Figure 9), and how refusal-heavy or non-instruction-tuned models participate (Appendices B.1 and B.5). Earlier memory, round-count, agent-count, evaluator, helpfulness, and category analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 introduces a fitted diversity–safety trend with a reported slope in Figure 9 and reports token usage as 2,104 ± 228 in Section 5.1. The meaning of the ± term is unspecified. Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for the safety results.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for new configurations and analyses. For the Gemma/Qwen/R1 triad, newly reported HarmBench total errors are 28.9% for SReD and 0.2% with GLTM; Appendix B.5 adds the Llama-Base trajectory of 33.8%, 43.3%, and 38.8%. Original first-triad table values remain, but Figure 3 exchanges the Llama and Phi curve assignments without explanation.

T1.justification: Figure 9 introduces a quantitative definition of semantic diversity using mean pairwise distance between embedded responses, calculated through cosine similarity. This supplements the retained safe/unsafe coexistence DIV measure. The framework equations and ER/AGR definitions remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central novelty claim and contributions remain automated debate-based safety refinement, vulnerability discovery, and learning through memory. Although v2 removes numerical reductions from the abstract, the introduction retains the 17.7% and over-23.5% claims. The broader experiments support the existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking safety refinement to semantic diversity and benefits beyond additional computation, and identifies participation limits for refusal-heavy and base models. It narrows GLTM's superiority claim to HarmBench, describing CoSafe performance as competitive. The cost limitation is recast as primarily training/adaptation overhead, replacing v1's explicit 3–4× wall-clock caveat.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents a 512-token response cap, random constitutional-rule selection, second-triad feedback/guardrail counts, and concrete NeMo runtime errors with troubleshooting guidance. Existing LoRA settings, embedding and retrieval details, prompts, and code access are retained. The quantified 3–4× latency estimate is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds MART and Rainbow Teaming to the red-teaming discussion, plus references concerning inference-time robustness, guaranteed-safe AI, and evaluator bias. These extend the research context while retaining the original positioning of debate, red-teaming, and memory as the work's distinctive combination.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are rewritten, and the results narrative is reorganized around computation and refinement mechanisms. Previously separate appendix analyses are consolidated and reordered into Appendix B, while detailed GLTM analysis moves from the main text to Appendix C.3. A language-model-use disclosure is also added.

P2.justification: v2 changes from two-column to single-column layout, redraws framework Figures 1–2, overlays and expands Figure 3, and merges v1 Figures 4–5 into v2 Figure 5. It adds budget, engagement, diversity, and comparison diagrams, expands tables with model blocks, and relocates multiple existing displays.

improvement.justification: The added model evaluations, output-token-matched Self-Critique comparison, and refusal/base-model analyses strengthen empirical support and clarify applicability while preserving v1's evidence. These gains are qualified: output-token matching leaves other computation unaccounted for, the earlier quantified latency caveat disappears, and Figure 3's unexplained Llama/Phi relabeling reduces reporting clarity. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
